title: Map bookkeeping: one settled line per ticket, out of scope never settled, map done from every path
story: Settled used to be able to show an old decision next to the current one, and a ticket closed as out of scope could also appear under Settled. Now each ticket has one settled line with its latest decision, and an out-of-scope ticket shows only under Out of scope until it is reopened, which also removes that line. Adding a ticket or merging that fails halfway can be repeated with the same words, and Grillo finishes the same ticket instead of making a second one. Two laptops changing the map at once now re-write on the fresh map, and Grillo says the map keeps changing if that keeps failing.

checks.criterion: A ticket closed after two decisions has exactly one settled line, holding the latest gist.
checks.steps: Open a made-up project with a map and an open ticket. Record two decisions on that ticket with different gists, using an agent or the own-time form. Close the ticket and open the Map tab.
checks.expected: One line for that ticket under Settled, showing the second gist.

checks.criterion: Closing a ticket as out of scope lists it only under Out of scope, even when it carried a decision.
checks.steps: On the Map tab, take an open ticket that has a decision and that nobody holds. Click Close as out of scope, type a made-up reason and confirm.
checks.expected: The ticket under Out of scope as <title>: <why> (#<number>), and no line for it under Settled.

checks.criterion: A merge that was undone and later decided on its own no longer reads as a duplicate.
checks.steps: Merge a made-up ticket into another on the Map tab. Reopen it (no reopen-ticket control exists on the map screen, so use an agent or a store-level path). Record a decision on it and close it.
checks.expected: The ticket's settled line shows that decision, and it does not read as a duplicate.

checks.criterion: A ticket create that fails halfway ends with every link after the retry.
checks.steps: On the Map tab, click Add ticket and fill in made-up text. Drop the network just after the issue appears on GitHub, so the dialog shows the error. Restore the network and click Add ticket again with the same words.
checks.expected: One issue only, a sub-issue of the map.
